title: Andromache's losses and plea
intro: Andromache recounts the destruction of her family, then offers Hector a practical defensive plan. Several familiar verbs appear in epic aorist forms.

notes.text: νηπίαχος, little / infant; ἄμμορος, without a share, hence unfortunate. Acc objects of ἐλεαίρεις on the preceding page.
χήρη, widow / bereft; σεῦ = σοῦ, gen of separation; εἰμί 1sg fut: I shall be widowed of you.
κατακτείνω 3pl fut, uncontracted: will kill. Recognize the κταν- stem.
ἐφορμάω aor pass-form ptc nom pl, with intransitive sense: rushing upon you together.
Potential optative: it would be better. κέρδιον neut comparative of κερδαλέος; δύω root aor inf, go down, with epic -μεναι.
ἀφαμαρτάνω aor ptc dat sg fem, agreeing with ἐμοί: for me, deprived of you. Gen σεῦ with the verb of losing.
χθών acc sg, earth; here going beneath the earth means dying.
Warmth / comfort / consolation; related to θάλπω, warm or cherish.
ἐφέπω 2sg aor subj mid, meet / encounter; πότμος, fate, especially death. ἐπεί + ἄν + subj: when you meet your doom.
ἄχεα, neut pl of ἄχος, grief; elided before οὐδέ. Contrasted with the absent θαλπωρή.
Possessive adjective, my, acc sg masc; an epic form beside ἐμόν.
ἐκπέρθω 3sg aor, utterly sacked; κατακτείνω 3sg aor, killed. Both compounds split in tmesis.
ναιετάω pres ptc, well inhabited; ὑψίπυλος, high-gated. Both describe Thebe.
ἐξεναρίζω 3sg aor, stripped the armor from a slain enemy.
σέβομαι 3sg aor mid, felt reverence / scruple. τό γε points to stripping the dead king, the act he shrank from.
κατακαίω 3sg aor, burned; ἔντεα dat pl, armor; δαιδάλεος, elaborately wrought.
χέω 3sg aor, heaped / poured; σῆμα, burial mound or grave marker. ἐπί: over him.
πτελέα, elm, acc pl; ὀρεστιάς, mountain-dwelling, nom pl fem, describing the nymphs.
κασίγνητος, sibling, here brothers; ἰῷ dat sg of ἴος, one; ἦμαρ dat sg ἤματι: on one day.
κίω 3pl impf, went; εἴσω with gen, into Hades' house. The house is understood.
καταπέφνω 3sg reduplicated aor, slew; φεν- / φον- family, as in φόνος, slaughter.
βοῦς dat pl; εἰλίπους, rolling-gaited / shambling, dat pl. ἐπί: tending or among the cattle.
ἀργεννός, white / shining; ὄϊς, sheep, dat pl epic -εσσι.
κτέαρ, possession: dat pl; here other spoils carried off with her mother.
ἄψ, back / again; ἀπολύω 3sg aor, released; ἄποινα neut pl, ransom. ἀπερείσια: boundless / immense.
Arrow-showering, epithet of Artemis. Her arrow marks the mother's death after her release.
θαλερός, flourishing / vigorous; παρακοίτης, bedfellow / husband. Hector replaces every family bond she has lost.
αὐτοῦ, here; μίμνω pres imperative, stay; τίθημι 2sg aor subj with μή, do not make. θήῃς is uncontracted.
ἵστημι 2sg aor imperative, station, transitive; ἐρινεός, wild fig tree, a landmark near the wall.
ἀμβατός, climbable; ἐπίδρομος, open to assault. ἔπλετο, 3sg past of πέλομαι, functions like was / is found to be.
πειράομαι 3pl aor mid, tried / made an attempt; elided -ντο before οἱ.
ἀμφί + acc names the leaders and their company; Αἴαντε acc dual, the two Ajaxes; Ἀτρεΐδας acc pl, Agamemnon and Menelaus.
